title: From Likelihood to Loss
tagline: Every loss function is a noise model in disguise — pick the density, read off the loss
summary: Choose a noise model for your residuals — Gaussian, Laplace, Uniform, or Student-t — and watch the loss function fall out as -log p(r). Three live panels stay in sync: the noise density, the per-residual loss curve, and a fitted line over real scatter. Add an outlier and see why squared error (Gaussian) breaks while absolute error (Laplace) and Student-t shrug it off.
highlights: See the identity loss = -log p(residual) come alive across four noise models in three synchronized panels.
Gaussian noise gives you squared error; Laplace gives absolute error; Uniform gives a hard interval barrier; Student-t gives a robust, heavy-tailed loss.
Toggle a single outlier and watch the least-squares line lurch while the robust fits barely move.
Drag slope and intercept sliders and read the total loss update live as the sum of per-point contributions.
Understand once and for all why MSE is sensitive to outliers and MAE is robust — it is entirely about the tails of the assumed noise.
